BiblicalUsage: Oiktirmos is mercy, pity, compassion, the tender mercies of God. Paul beseeches the Romans by the mercies of God in Romans 12:1, and calls God the Father of mercies in 2 Corinthians 1:3. The same word is the appeal in Philippians 2:1, if there be any bowels and mercies, and the clothing of the elect in Colossians 3:12, put on bowels of mercies.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the mercies of God are the ground of everything Paul asks, because he never commands without first remembering what God has done. My position is that mercy is not a mood of God, it is His name: the Father of mercies, and His children wear it.
